questions.question: A man starts from his house and travelling at 30 km/h, he reaches his office late by 10 minutes, and travelling at 24 km/h, he reaches his office late by 18 minutes. The distance (in km) from his house to his office is∶
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the formula: Distance = [Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds] × Time Difference

Speed₁ = 30 km/h, Speed₂ = 24 km/h

Time Difference = 18 min − 10 min = 8 min = 8 ÷ 60 hours

Distance = [ (30 × 24) ÷ (30 − 24) ] × (8 ÷ 60)

Distance = [ 720 ÷ 6 ] × (2 ÷ 15) = 120 × (2 ÷ 15) = 8 × 2 = 16 km

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ (S₁) = 30 km/h, Arrival = 10 min late

Speed₂ (S₂) = 24 km/h, Arrival = 18 min late

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂| ] × ΔT

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af575b4b6322aba9f124c1abb20b2a6bf94fc8372e8f4a4f17d8be0aedd0a2c9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the actual time to reach be 'T' minutes.

⇒ Time taken at 30 km/h (T₁) = T + 10 min

⇒ Time taken at 24 km/h (T₂) = T + 18 min

⇒ Time difference (ΔT) = T₂ − T₁ = (T + 18) − (T + 10) = 8 min

⇒ Convert ΔT to hours: ΔT = 8 ÷ 60 = 2 ÷ 15 hours

⇒ Using speed-distance relation: Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ D = [ (30 × 24) ÷ (30 − 24) ] × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = [ 720 ÷ 6 ] × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = 120 × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = 8 × 2 = 16 km

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂ or S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.

Time Difference Rule

If one speed leads to being 'x' minutes late and another to 'y' minutes late, the time difference ΔT = |x − y|. If one is late and another is early, ΔT = x + y.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If a person covers the same distance at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the whole journey is 2S₁S₂ ÷ (S₁ + S₂).</p

questions.question: If the diameter of the base of a right circular cylinder is reduced by 33(1)/(3)\% and its height is doubled, then the volume of the cylinder will:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Reduction in diameter (or radius) = 33 1/3% = 1/3. Initial Radius : Final Radius = 3 : 2.

Height is doubled. Initial Height : Final Height = 1 : 2.

Volume (V) ∝ r² × h.

Initial Volume (V₁) = 3² × 1 = 9 units.

Final Volume (V₂) = 2² × 2 = 8 units.

Decrease in Volume = (9 − 8) / 9 = 1/9 = 11 1/9%.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by 11 1/9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduction in diameter = 33 1/3% = 1/3 of original.

New height (h₂) = 2 × original height (h₁).

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder (V) = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/785a40428da6f685dd438ef46c55fc7895c2b0a2fd805893a023030936263852.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original radius = r₁ and original height = h₁.

⇒ New radius (r₂) = r₁ − (1/3)r₁ = (2/3)r₁.

⇒ New height (h₂) = 2h₁.

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = π × (r₁)² × h₁.

⇒ Final Volume (V₂) = π × (2r₁/3)² × 2h₁.

⇒ V₂ = π × (4r₁²/9) × 2h₁ = (8/9) × πr₁²h₁.

⇒ Percentage change = [(V₂ − V₁) / V₁] × 100.

⇒ Percentage change = [(8/9 − 1) / 1] × 100 = −1/9 × 100 = −11 1/9%.

⇒ Negative sign indicates a decrease.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by 11 1/9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Dependency

For a cylinder, Volume is proportional to the square of the radius and directly proportional to the height (V ∝ r²h).

Percentage to Fraction

Common conversions: 33 1/3% = 1/3, 11 1/9% = 1/9, 66 2/3% = 2/3, 14 2/8% = 1/7.

Successive Percentage Change

For changes in r (twice) and h (once), the net change is the product of their multiplier factors: (1 − 1/3) × (1 − 1/3) × (2) = 2/3 × 2/3 × 2 = 8/9.</p

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 14,395.20 at 9.25% p.a. simple interest in 5.4 years. What will be the simple interest on the same sum at 8.6% p.a. in 4.5 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total interest % for first case = 9.25% × 5.4 = 49.95%

Amount % = 100% + 49.95% = 149.95%

Total interest % for second case = 8.6% × 4.5 = 38.7%

Required SI = (14395.20 ÷ 149.95) × 38.7

Required SI = 96 × 38.7 = 3715.20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,715.20.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Amount (A₁) = Rs. 14,395.20, Rate (R₁) = 9.25%, Time (T₁) = 5.4 years

Target: SI for Rate (R₂) = 8.6%, Time (T₂) = 4.5 years

Formula: Amount = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/131081f8aa36e75d2d56634b861509d2797db0f41934343a1e02b66d66baffb5.png] 

⇒ Amount (A₁) = P × (1 + (R₁ × T₁) ÷ 100)

⇒ 14395.20 = P × (1 + (9.25 × 5.4) ÷ 100)

⇒ 14395.20 = P × (1 + 49.95 ÷ 100) = P × 1.4995

⇒ P = 14395.20 ÷ 1.4995 = Rs. 9600

⇒ SI₂ = (P × R₂ × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (9600 × 8.6 × 4.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 96 × 38.7

⇒ SI₂ = Rs. 3715.20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,715.20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The basic formula for Simple Interest is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate per annum, and T is Time in years.

Effective Rate of Interest

Total interest percentage over T years is (R × T)%. This can be directly added to 100% to find the Amount percentage.

Amount Calculation

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Interest (SI). In terms of percentage, A = P(100 + RT) ÷ 100.</p

questions.question: A solid cube is cut into three cuboids of same volumes. What is the ratio of the surface area of the cube to the sum of the surface areas of any two of the cuboids so formed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the side of the cube be 3 units (chosen because 3 is easily divisible by 3).

Surface Area of original cube = 6 × (side)² = 6 × 3² = 54 sq. units.

Dimensions of each of the three identical cuboids = 3 × 3 × (3 ÷ 3) = 3 × 3 × 1.

Surface Area of one cuboid = 2(3×3 + 3×1 + 1×3) = 2(9 + 3 + 3) = 30 sq. units.

Sum of Surface Areas of two cuboids = 30 × 2 = 60 sq. units.

Required Ratio = 54 : 60 = 9 : 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A solid cube is cut into 3 equal volume cuboids.

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Cube = 6a²

Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5ec570ae599920b097398bb7c784d75a40a28a1d3a8c236b661f97e5bcdf1c5.png] 

Let the side of the cube be 'a'.

⇒ Surface Area of Cube (S₁) = 6a²

⇒ When cut into three equal volumes, dimensions of each cuboid: length = a, breadth = a, height = a/3

⇒ Surface Area of one cuboid = 2[ (a × a) + (a × a/3) + (a/3 × a) ]

⇒ Surface Area of one cuboid = 2[ a² + a²/3 + a²/3 ]

⇒ Surface Area of one cuboid = 2[ (3a² + a² + a²) / 3 ] = 2[ 5a²/3 ] = 10a²/3

⇒ Sum of surface areas of any two cuboids (S₂) = 2 × (10a²/3) = 20a²/3

⇒ Required Ratio = S₁ : S₂

⇒ Ratio = 6a² : (20a²/3)

⇒ Ratio = 18a² : 20a²

⇒ Ratio = 9 : 10

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area Increase on Cutting

Whenever a solid is cut, the total volume remains constant, but the total surface area increases because new faces are exposed. For every parallel cut, two new faces (equal to the cross-sectional area) are created.

General Formula for 'n' Slices

If a cube is cut into 'n' identical cuboids by 'n−1' parallel cuts, the total surface area of all 'n' cuboids = 6a² + 2(n−1)a² = (2n+4)a².

Volume of Cuboid

Volume of a cuboid is given by Length × Breadth × Height. When cutting a cube of side 'a' into 'n' equal parts, the volume of each part is a³/n.</p

questions.question: 40 litres of 60% concentration of an acid solution is added to 35 litres of 80% concentration of the acid solution. What is the concentration of acid in the new solution?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of quantity of solution A to solution B = 40 : 35 = 8 : 7.

Lower concentration = 60%, Higher concentration = 80%. Difference = 20%.

New Concentration = Lower % + [Ratio parts of higher / Total ratio parts] × Difference

New Concentration = 60% + [7 / (8 + 7)] × 20% = 60% + 28/3% = 60% + 9 1/3% = 69 1/3%.

**∴ The correct answer is 69 1/3%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity 1 (Q₁) = 40 L, Concentration 1 (C₁) = 60%

Quantity 2 (Q₂) = 35 L, Concentration 2 (C₂) = 80%

**Formula:**

New Concentration = (Q₁ × C₁ + Q₂ × C₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5729ad17b3be2851d000e174b4b774e262076dc6c94cda427c4dae0e19ef5125.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount of acid in first solution = 40 × (60/100) = 24 L

⇒ Amount of acid in second solution = 35 × (80/100) = 28 L

⇒ Total acid in the mixture = 24 + 28 = 52 L

⇒ Total quantity of the new solution = 40 + 35 = 75 L

⇒ Final concentration = (52 / 75) × 100%

⇒ Final concentration = (52 × 4) / 3 = 208 / 3 %

⇒ Final concentration = 69 1/3%

**∴ The correct answer is 69 1/3%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It states that the ratio of the weights of two items mixed is inversely proportional to the difference of their prices/concentrations from the mean value: (Quantity 1 / Quantity 2) = (C₂ − Mean) / (Mean − C₁).

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages are combined, the combined average is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) / (n₁ + n₂).

Mixture of Multiple Solutions

For mixing three or more solutions, the same principle applies: Total mass of solute ÷ Total mass of solution × 100.</p

questions.question: The area of the base of a right circular cone is 400π and its height is 15 cm. The curved surface area of the cone (in cm²) is∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Base Area = πr² = 400π ⇒ r = 20 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5) × 5 → (15, 20, 25).

Height (h) = 15, Radius (r) = 20 ⇒ Slant height (l) = 25 cm.

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l = π × 20 × 25 = 500π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 500 π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Area of the base = 400π cm², Height of the cone (h) = 15 cm.

**Formula Used:** Area of base = πr², Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²), Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a3517760d4b2be6f89c81970fc37a8c27107cf98641c833c2aa9c69f2b81cdc.png] 

⇒ Area of base = π × r² = 400π

⇒ r² = 400

⇒ r = √400 = 20 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

⇒ l = √(20² + 15²) = √(400 + 225)

⇒ l = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π × r × l

⇒ CSA = π × 20 × 25 = 500π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 500 π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the base: TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a right circular cone is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height: V = (1/3) × πr²h.

Pythagorean Relation

In a right circular cone, the height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) always satisfy l² = r² + h².</p

questions.question: A right circular solid cone of radius 3.2 cm and height 7.2 cm is melted and recast into a right circular cylinder of height 9.6 cm. What is the diameter of the base of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a solid is melted and recast, the Volume remains constant.

Volume of Cone = Volume of Cylinder ⇒ (1/3) × r₁² × h₁ = r₂² × h₂

(1/3) × 3.2 × 3.2 × 7.2 = r₂² × 9.6

3.2 × 3.2 × 2.4 = r₂² × 9.6 ⇒ r₂² = (3.2 × 3.2) ÷ 4

r₂ = 3.2 ÷ 2 = 1.6 cm

Diameter = 2 × 1.6 = 3.2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cone (r₁) = 3.2 cm

Height of cone (h₁) = 7.2 cm

Height of cylinder (h₂) = 9.6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Volume of Cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3aa2e302061e4d38c681137c5be1a633829e225bae95f82b31fe906b721aefd0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of cylinder = Volume of cone

⇒ π × r₂² × h₂ = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h₁

⇒ r₂² × 9.6 = (1/3) × (3.2)² × 7.2

⇒ r₂² × 9.6 = (3.2 × 3.2) × (7.2 ÷ 3)

⇒ r₂² × 9.6 = 3.2 × 3.2 × 2.4

⇒ r₂² = (3.2 × 3.2 × 2.4) ÷ 9.6

⇒ r₂² = (3.2 × 3.2) ÷ 4

⇒ r₂ = √(3.2² ÷ 2²) = 3.2 ÷ 2

⇒ r₂ = 1.6 cm

⇒ Diameter of base = 2 × r₂

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 1.6 = 3.2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cone

The total surface area of a cone is given by πr(r + l), where l is the slant height √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

The lateral or curved surface area of a cylinder is 2πrh, and the total surface area is 2πr(r + h).

Conservation of Volume

In melting and recasting problems, the volume of the material remains the same, provided there is no wastage during the process.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2 cm.**</p

questions.question: 4 men and 5 women can complete a work in 15 days, whereas 9 men and 6 women can do it in 10 days. To complete the same work in 7 days, how many women should assist 4 men?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Work Equated: 15 × (4 Men + 5 Women) = 10 × (9 Men + 6 Women)

60 Men + 75 Women = 90 Men + 60 Women ⇒ 30 Men = 15 Women ⇒ 2 Men = 1 Woman

Total Work in Women-days = (4 Men + 5 Women) × 15 = (2 Women + 5 Women) × 15 = 105 Women-units

To finish in 7 days, daily capacity required = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 Women

Available capacity from 4 Men = 2 Women. Additional women needed = 15 − 2 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 women.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: (4M + 5W) complete work in 15 days.

Case 2: (9M + 6W) complete work in 10 days.

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁) = (M₂ × D₂)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Group A (4M + 5W)
 15
 30
 2
 
 

 Group B (9M + 6W)
 10
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Group A = 2 units/day ⇒ 4M + 5W = 2

⇒ Efficiency of Group B = 3 units/day ⇒ 9M + 6W = 3

⇒ Equating normalized capacity: 3 × (4M + 5W) = 2 × (9M + 6W)

⇒ 12M + 15W = 18M + 12W ⇒ 6M = 3W ⇒ 1 Woman = 2 Men

⇒ Total Work = (4M + 5W) × 15 = (2W + 5W) × 15 = 105 Women-units

⇒ Required capacity for 7 days = Total Work ÷ Days = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 Women

⇒ Team required = 4 Men + x Women = 15 Women

⇒ 2 Women + x Women = 15 Women ⇒ x = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 women.**

**__Additional Information__**

Man-Day Formula

For a constant piece of work, the relationship is M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂, where M is number of workers, D is days, and H is hours.

Efficiency and Time

The time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency of the workers. Efficiency Ratio = 1 ÷ Time Ratio.

Work Equivalence

When different types of workers (men, women, children) are involved, first establish an efficiency relationship (e.g., 1 Man = k Women) to convert the entire problem into a single unit.</p

questions.question: (sec ϕ – tan ϕ)² (1 + sin ϕ)² ÷ sin² ϕ = ?

Use the Angle Substitution method: Let ϕ = 45°.

Then, sec 45° = √2, tan 45° = 1, and sin 45° = 1/√2.

Substitute these into the expression: (√2 − 1)² × (1 + 1/√2)² ÷ (1/√2)².

= [(√2 − 1) × ((√2 + 1)/√2)]² × 2 = [(2 − 1)/√2]² × 2 = (1/2) × 2 = 1.

Checking options for ϕ = 45°: cot² 45° = 1² = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is cot² ϕ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

questions.question: 5 years ago, the ratio of the age of A to that of B was 4 ∶ 5. Five years hence, the ratio of the age of A to that of B will be 6 ∶ 7. If, at present, C is 10 years younger than B, then what will be the ratio of the present age of A to that of C?

⇒ Difference in A's ratio units = 6 − 4 = 2 units

⇒ A's present age = 20 + 5 = 25 years

⇒ B's age (5 years ago) = 5 × 5 = 25 years

⇒ B's present age = 25 + 5 = 30 years

⇒ C's present age = 30 − 10 = 20 years

questions.question: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 80% of this price, then there will be a loss of 10%. What is the percent profit when the article is sold at the original selling price?

Let the Original Selling Price be S and Cost Price be CP.

New Selling Price = 80% of S = 0.8S.

According to the question, 0.8S results in a 10% loss → 0.8S = 90% of CP.

Ratio of S : CP = 90 : 80 = 9 : 8.

Profit at Original SP = (9 − 8) ÷ 8 × 100 = 1 ÷ 8 × 100 = 12.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 1/2 %.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New Selling Price = 80% of Original Selling Price

Loss percentage at New Selling Price = 10%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100

⇒ At a 10% loss, the New Selling Price = 100 − 10 = ₹90.

⇒ It is given that this ₹90 is 80% of the Original Selling Price.

⇒ 0.80 × Original SP = 90

⇒ Original SP = 90 ÷ 0.80 = 900 ÷ 8 = ₹112.5

⇒ Profit at Original SP = Original SP − CP = 112.5 − 100 = ₹12.5

⇒ Profit percentage = (12.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 12.5%

⇒ 12.5% = 12 1/2 %

**∴ The correct answer is 12 1/2 %.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. If SP > CP, it is profit; if SP < CP, it is loss.

Common fractions: 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, 3/4 = 75%, and 1/5 = 20%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 800 and it is sold at a discount of 19%. If there is a gain of 8%, then by what percent above the cost price was the article marked?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio formula between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP).

CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 19) : (100 + 8) = 81 : 108

Simplifying the ratio: 3 : 4 (Dividing by 27)

Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33 1/3%

**∴ The correct answer is 33 1/3%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Marked Price (MP) = ₹800, Discount = 19%, Profit = 8%.

Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100 and CP = SP × 100 / (100 + P%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e61cf505cd743f841288cd52af80dce932f25454ffd8ccaf962ade523804b168.png] 

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 800 × (100 − 19) / 100

⇒ SP = 800 × 81 / 100 = 8 × 81 = ₹648

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) / (100 + 8)

⇒ CP = (648 × 100) / 108 = 6 × 100 = ₹600

⇒ Markup Amount = MP − CP = 800 − 600 = ₹200

⇒ Markup % = (Markup Amount / CP) × 100

⇒ Markup % = (200 / 600) × 100 = 1/3 × 100 = 33 1/3%

**∴ The correct answer is 33 1/3%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Marked Price Relationship

The ratio is given by CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This is the most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It represents the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.
